schemes.description: Multidisciplinary teams of Queen Mary undergraduates act as consultants on live problems set by external host organisations (businesses, charities, social enterprises, not-for-profits; UK and international). Project types include research and analysis, marketing, sustainability, business strategy and data/customer insight. Teams meet the host at set-up, mid-project and final stages, are supported by a Queen Mary supervisor, and present findings and recommendations to the client as a presentation and short written report. Formats: autumn programme (Oct-Nov, weekly training), one-day hackathons (Feb-May), two-week Summer Sprint (June).
schemes.admin_host: Careers and Enterprise (Student Consultancy Project team); part of the SKETCH knowledge-exchange programme
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Open to all Queen Mary undergraduates from any academic school, including medicine and dentistry; QMUL Bursary recipients prioritised.
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Undergraduates only; no prior consultancy experience needed; application and selection.
schemes.credit_assessment: Not stated as credit-bearing; no credit evidenced.
schemes.duration: Autumn programme Oct-Nov; hackathons one day; Summer Sprint two weeks
schemes.delivery_format: Team consultancy projects with training sessions and supervisor support; some formats short (hackathon).
schemes.project_evidence: Live problems with defined outputs: presentation and short written report with recommendations to the host (sources 1, 2).
schemes.group_evidence: Multidisciplinary student teams working together on one host project (sources 1, 2).
schemes.employer_evidence: Host organisations (any UK/international business, charity, social enterprise or not-for-profit) supply the problem, meet teams at set-up, mid-project and final stages and receive the presentation/report (source 2). External hosts are the documented norm.
schemes.partner_role: Supplies live challenge, attends check-ins, receives final presentation and report. A minority of SBM-run SCP teams research university-internal questions (access and participation work, source 3), which are internal rather than external.
schemes.deliverable: Presentation and short written report with findings and recommendations to the client

profile_md:
**Provision found.** Queen Mary's clearest provision is distributed across SBM and the SKETCH student knowledge-exchange programme rather than institution-wide curriculum. The only University-wide route is the **Student Consultancy Project** (Careers): selective, extracurricular, multidisciplinary undergraduate teams working for external business, charity and social-enterprise hosts and presenting a report and presentation to them (autumn programme, one-day hackathons, two-week summer sprint). **qHeritage** (History, open to current QM students) and **qNomics Client Advisory** (Economics and Finance, third-year UG and PG) are further extracurricular team-client routes with confirmed 2026/27 recruitment.

**Curricular routes.** In the Business School, **BUS380 Social Impact Project** (15 credits, Level 6, optional) has teams consult for charities/social enterprises, with a Tower Hamlets Council brief and Town Hall presentation described; **BUSM250** (60 credits) and the **MSc Entrepreneurship and Innovation capstone** (clients ViWipe, FlowSense, Decentials, Clean Break; completed June 2026) place PG students with live clients. **Real World Impact Projects** span SBM and Society & Environment.

**Limits.** SBM Consult uses internal university clients (C not met). MEng group design projects are only "frequently" sponsored; EECS industry MSc projects are individual. Science, Law and Medicine/Dentistry yielded no qualifying group client route. Many pages are undated, so several curricular routes are not confirmed current. Participation counts are rarely published (qNomics reported 18 SMEs supported in 2025).
gaps: BUS380, BUSM250 and Real World Impact Projects lack dated 2025/26 delivery evidence. Group working for the E&I capstone not established. Numbers of participants/teams not found for most schemes. Further departmental instances likely (SEMS/EECS sponsored projects, DEN327, SKETCH strands, Natural Capital/Water MSc partner projects). Science schools and medical/dental programmes yielded nothing but were searched only via two broad queries each. Search results were summaries, not page text.
